base: main d34a00eb (WP87 warm API, WP90 trapped-chain guard default since 8cb33fbf, WP91 warm session); no library change
question: Does the WP93 post-hoc estimator (the likelihood-reweighted pool of the last H ticks' warm draws with the importance weights normalised within each lag group) meet the WP88 quote rule at K in {20, 50, 200} transitions per chain per tick on the WP84 simulated series AND on the real BTC-perpetual bar-close series, against a gated reference at every tick?

model.source: market_uncertainty_v1 sv_prototype Target, P=1 intercept, K=0 flow (WP84 target; density code byte-identical to WP88 / WP93, checked against models/sv.stan through BridgeStan before WP88's freeze)

sim.source: WP84 simulate.py, seed 84084, 1,100 returns + truth h; byte-identical to online_sv_quote_v1/models/data.json, online_sv_quote_v2/models/data-sim.json and tick_pooling_v1/models/data.json

real.source: WP88 real_data.py: 682 Deribit BTC-PERPETUAL 30-minute bar-close log returns reconstructed from the archived rolling windows of market_uncertainty_v1 (sv-historical-rolling-v1/evidence.zip); byte-identical to online_sv_quote_v2/models/data-real.json; same priors, no rescaling, no truth h

stream.posterior_at_tick_t: first N+t returns; tick t's new return is y[N+t-1] (0-indexed)

quantities.h_next: mu + rho (h_last - mu) + exp(log_sigma) eps, eps[c,j] = default_rng(eps_seed_base+tick).normal(size=(4,20000))[c,j] (chain index c of the arm or reference; the WP84/WP88/WP93 common stream, reused on purpose: it defines the quantity)
reported: arm's own quantile MCSE (arviz) of P50/P95 at H = 1
bulk ESS and R-hat of h_next at H = 1
weight ESS of the pool and of every lag group
own MCSE of the pooled P50 (chain-split, below)
fraction of pooled weight inside the reference 90 % interval of h_next
quantities.quantile: weighted quantile by linear interpolation of the midpoint CDF (sorted values x_i with normalised weights w_i, c_i = sum_{k<=i} w_k - w_i/2, q(p) = interp(p, c, x), clamped at the ends; uniform weights = Hyndman-Fan type 5); used for every arm AND for the reference (WP93's definition)

reference.arm: oWALNUTS defaults 4 x 2000/20000 per tick, best-of-16 starts, Limits::admit_worst_case + max_result_bytes_unchecked(2 GiB); the trapped-chain guard is the sampler default on this base (first reference under it: WP88's and WP93's references ran before the flip commit 8cb33fbf, WP93's preregistration misdescribed its base on this point)
reference.gate: drop chains named by a WarmupStep or SampledLogDensity chain warning; pass iff >= min_chains remain AND rank R-hat(h_next) over the remaining chains <= max_rhat (arviz 0.23.4) -- the WP88 gate unchanged
reference.seed_rule: attempt a at tick t of dataset d: seed_base[d]*1000 + t + 200*a; attempt 1 only when attempt 0 fails the gate (part of the cell, not a rerun)
reference.gate_failed: a tick failing both attempts is unscored and counts as a FAILED tick for every configuration scored there
reference.ticks: 0..100, every tick, on both datasets (WP93: every 10th tick cannot resolve the rule; the reference depends on the data only, so one reference per dataset serves the three seeds: 202 reference ticks)
reference.split: ref-<d>-lo = ticks 0-50, ref-<d>-hi = ticks 51-100 (scheduling only; the seed rule does not depend on the split)

arms.warm: LIBRARY path (WP93 harness unchanged): gated tick-0 default fit 4 x 1000/1000 (see tick0_gate), Posterior::warm_state(), then per tick WarmState::extend_to(3+n, 0.0, 1.0) and Sampler::run_warm with draws(K), seed = seed*1000003 + 16*tick (chain c on seed+c), threads 4, Limits::admit_worst_case; the result's warm_state() is the next state; no re-adaptation
arms.tick0_gate: attempt 0 at the cell seed; if a chain is named by a WarmupStep/SampledLogDensity warning (a trapped chain), one more attempt at seed + 10; the last attempt's flagged chains are dropped from the carried state (WP88 rule), fewer than 2 chains left = the cell fails (a result). The tick-0 fit is outside the latency statistics.
arms.draws_stored: per tick [chain][draw][4] little-endian f32 = mu, log_sigma, beta, h_last (= h_{N+t}, the latent of the newest return; tick 0 too). These four are everything the re-propagation needs: the AR(1) is Markov in h, rho and nu are fixed, so earlier latents never enter; the z coordinates are not stored.

pooling.pool: at tick t the pool holds the draws of ticks max(1, t-H+1)..t (all kept chains, all K draws per chain); tick 0 (the 1,000-draw full fit) is never pooled; for t < H the pool is shorter (the online cold start), those ticks are scored like any other and the pass share over ticks >= 20 (every pool full) is also reported
pooling.control: asis at H = 1: the newest tick's own h_next draws, uniform weights (the WP88 / WP93 estimator; at H = 1 every estimator coincides with it)
pooling.estimator: pf-lagnorm (THE ESTIMATOR UNDER TEST, WP93 posthoc/pf_lagnorm.py reproduced exactly): for lag j = t - s in 0..H-1 the tick-s draws are particles (mu_i, sigma_i = exp(log_sigma_i), beta_i, h_i = h_{N+s}). Lag 0: value = the tick-t h_next from the common eps stream, log-weight 0. Lag j >= 1: fresh noise eps_i,m ~ N(0,1), m = 0..j, from default_rng(prop_seed_base[d] + t) (one stream per tick; lag groups drawn in increasing j, each as normal(size=(n_j, j+1))); for m = 0..j-1: h_i <- mu_i + rho (h_i - mu_i) + sigma_i eps_i,m, then logw_i += log t_nu(y[N+s+m] - beta_i; 0, exp(h_i/2)) (the return that arrived at tick s+m+1); the value is h_next,i = mu_i + rho (h_i - mu_i) + sigma_i eps_i,j. Within lag group j the importance weights are self-normalised, v_i = exp(logw_i - max) / sum, and multiplied by the time weight w_j; the pool concatenates the lag groups' values and weights, normalises, and the weighted quantile (midpoint CDF) of sigma_next = exp(h_next/2) gives P50 and P95. The lag-0 group is the exact current draws.

weighting.primary: exp: w_j = 2^(-j / (H/2)) (half-life H/2; the WP93 post-hoc weighting of the K = 50 result at both H and of the K = 20, H = 20 result at 95.3 %)
weighting.secondary: uniform: w_j = 1 (reported; the WP93 post hoc gave it 95.0 % at K = 20, H = 20 and a drift miss at K = 50, H = 20)

pooling.weight_ess: per lag group: 1 / sum(v_i^2) of the within-group normalised weights (reported as a fraction of the group's draws, median over ticks); per pool: 1 / sum(w_i^2) of the pool-normalised weights
pooling.own_mcse: chain-split own MCSE of the pooled P50 (no reference needed): the pooled P50 is recomputed from each kept chain's draws alone (same lags, importance weights normalised within that chain's lag group, same time weights); MCSE = sd over the C chains (ddof 1) / sqrt(C), reported relative to the pooled P50 (median over ticks). At H = 1 the arviz quantile MCSE (WP88 / WP93) is reported as well.
pooling.configurations: per dataset and K: asis H = 1 (control), pf-lagnorm H in {10, 20} x {exp, uniform}: 5 per (dataset, K), 30 in all, each scored on the same 300 ticks of its dataset
pooling.pooling_time: the analysis-side arithmetic per tick and configuration (numpy): the re-propagation of the lags < H plus the weighting and the weighted quantile; timed per tick and added to the library call for the latency rule

accuracy.rule: a scored tick passes iff |P50 sigma_next rel. error| <= 0.02 AND |P95 rel. error| <= 0.05 vs the gated reference AND no stuck chain at the newest tick AND (library-call wall of the newest tick + pooling arithmetic of the configuration) < threshold
accuracy.stuck_chain: a chain of the newest tick's draws is stuck when the median of its log_sigma draws is > 1.0 from the gated reference's median log_sigma, or the median of its h_last draws > 2.0 from the reference's median h_last (WP84/WP88 census rule)
accuracy.scored_ticks: reference ticks 1..100 of every seed (100 per seed, 300 pooled per dataset) for every configuration; tick 0 scored separately
accuracy.pass: a configuration (dataset, K, H, weighting) passes iff its pass share is >= 0.95 pooled over the three seeds (>= 285/300) AND >= 0.90 in every seed (>= 90/100) AND drift is within bound in every seed
accuracy.largest_tolerance: per (dataset, K, H, weighting): the first pair (ordered P50 then P95) on the grid P50 in {1, 2, 5, 10} % x P95 in {2, 5, 10, 20} % with >= 95 % pooled and >= 90 % per seed (accuracy and stuck chain only; no latency or drift condition; WP88's definition)

latency.library: wall per tick of the library call: from Sv::new (new target) through WarmState::extend_to and Sampler::run_warm to warm_state() taken; draw file writing excluded
latency.pooling: wall of the analysis-side pooling arithmetic for that configuration (see pooling.pooling_time)

drift.statistic: per seed and configuration: mean signed P50 relative error over late scored ticks (tick >= 70) minus over early scored ticks (1 <= tick <= 30)

decision_rule: The README may say 'K = <k> per tick with a reweighted pool of <H> ticks meets the quote rule on simulated and real returns in <ms>' only for a (K, H, exp) configuration that passes (the pass definition) on all three seeds of BOTH datasets; <ms> is the median library + pooling latency per dataset. The primary answer is the smallest such K and its H. Otherwise the README names, per dataset, the largest tolerance met per (K, H) and the measured pass shares; a configuration passing on one dataset only is reported as such and may not be named in the headline sentence. The uniform weighting is a reported secondary and cannot carry the headline.

predictions.P1: H = 1 control reproduces WP88 / WP93: sim K = 200 passes (94-98 % pooled), K = 50 fails (48-60 %), K = 20 fails (25-45 %); real K = 200 fails (78-90 %), K = 50 (30-48 %), K = 20 (12-30 %)
predictions.P2: sim, pf-lagnorm exp: K = 200 passes at H = 10 and H = 20 (99-100 %); K = 50 passes at both H (94-98 %; P(both pass) 0.7); K = 20 at H = 20 reaches 92-97 % (P(pass) 0.5) and at H = 10 fails (82-90 %)
predictions.P3: real, pf-lagnorm exp: K = 200 passes at H = 10 and 20 (96-100 %); K = 50 at H = 20 reaches 92-97 % (P(pass) 0.4) and at H = 10 fails (86-93 %); K = 20 fails at both H (72-88 %). Reasoning: on real returns WP88's K = 200 as-is (ESS about 1,000) reached 83 % with an own P50 MCSE of 1.25 % against 0.93 % on sim, so real needs about 1.8x the weight ESS of sim; the K = 20, H = 20 pool has about the ESS of K = 200 as-is
predictions.P4: the smallest K passing on BOTH datasets is 200 (P 0.6) or 50 (P 0.4); K = 20 does not pass both (P 0.9); if the headline sentence is allowed at all it reads K = 200 with H = 10 (sim 75-90 ms + pooling, real 280-340 ms + pooling) or K = 50 with H = 20
predictions.P5: uniform and exp pass shares within 3 points of each other on every (dataset, K, H); the uniform drift statistic is larger in magnitude than the exponential one on most seeds at H = 20
predictions.P6: weight efficiency per lag group (sim, any K): lag 1 95-98 %, lag 9 65-75 %, lag 19 40-50 % (WP93 post hoc: 97 / 71 / 45 %); real lower by 5-15 points at lags >= 9 (fatter return surprises); pool wESS at K = 20, H = 20 exp 900-1,100 on sim
predictions.P7: latency medians (4 pinned cores, co-tenanted): library call sim K = 20 7-10 ms, K = 50 18-24, K = 200 75-90; real K = 20 28-40 ms, K = 50 70-95, K = 200 280-340; the pooling arithmetic at H = 20 is 1-10 ms at every K (< 15 ms at K = 200); library + pooling under 0.4 s on 100 % of ticks except real K = 200 (97-100 %)
predictions.P8: signed bias of pf-lagnorm: |signed mean P50 error| <= 0.3 % and |signed mean P95 error| <= 0.5 % at K = 200 on both datasets; drift within 0.5 pp on every seed of every passing configuration
predictions.P9: gated reference under the guard default: 0-3 of 202 ticks drop a flagged chain (WP93: 7/101 sim without the guard, WP88: 2/51 real without it), 0-1 need the second seed, 0 fail both; 0-2 of the 18 tick-0 fits need the retry
predictions.P10: chain-split own MCSE of the pooled P50 (median over ticks): sim K = 20 H = 20 0.7-1.1 %, K = 50 H = 20 0.45-0.7 %, K = 200 H = 20 0.2-0.4 %; real 1.2-1.5x these; configurations pass once it is below about 1 %

budget: about 110 lane-minutes: references 202 ticks (sim 101 x ~18 s driver wall as WP93 = 30 min, real 101 x ~42 s as WP88's 35 s sampler wall + driver = 71 min), warm cells 18 x 10-40 s = 6 min; two lanes in parallel (lane 3: sim warm + both lo halves about 56 min; lane 4: real warm + both hi halves about 55 min), about 1 h wall after the build; analysis about 5 min
execution: lanes 3 and 4 (cores 8-11 and 12-15) of the shared c7a.4xlarge, taskset-pinned, RAYON_NUM_THREADS=4 OMP_NUM_THREADS=1, co-tenanted with WP94 on cores 0-7 and with each other: walls are 'pinned, co-tenanted'; accuracy and gradient counts unaffected. Started only after WP96 released cores 8-15 (pgrep -f warm_drift empty)
discipline: two lanes run in parallel, cells sequential within a lane in protocol order (run_cells.py plan); a started cell is never rerun (an existing output directory is skipped); failures are results; the reference's second attempt and the tick-0 retry are parts of the cell
